description: Narrow gates for experimental SET2 short-sequence emission, mined from the SF2 Set cluster deep dive. Off-by-default. Each gate is a (condition -> tactic) rule. Only SET_ITE_SIMP has >=2-theorem mined support; the others are speculative structural gates carried for measurement only. NEVER modifies RC1 / NS24.

match_semantics.fields: Gate conditions are evaluated over (theorem full_name, goal/state pretty-print). All conditions in a gate are ANDed.

predicates.name_or_ns_has_set: 'Set' appears in the theorem full_name or namespace
predicates.goal_has_set_relation: goal contains a Set membership/equality/order token: one of = , ∈ , ⊆ , ⊂ , ∩ , ∪ , \ , ∅
predicates.no_multiset_target: 'Multiset' does NOT appear in name or goal
predicates.not_arithmetic_only: goal does not look like a pure Nat/Int arithmetic goal (no Set/membership tokens present would fail name_or_ns_has_set anyway)

gates.rationale: Only mined template with >=2-theorem support and NO theorem-specific symbols. Pure tactic; unfolds Set.ite then closes by simp. Baselines (simp/simp_all/aesop/classical<;>aesop) all failed on both wins.
gates.expected_safety: high — requires both Set context AND an ite token; cannot fire on Nat/Multiset or non-ite Set goals.
gates.known_risks: On Set.ite goals that need more than definitional unfold (e.g. ite_inter, ite_inter_self) simp [Set.ite] makes no progress / fails — emission is cheap and harmless but not always sufficient.

mined_support.note: no deep-dive win was the pure ext<;>simp form

gates.rationale: Structural Set-equality extensionality. Speculative: carried to measure on holdout, NOT mined-supported.
gates.expected_safety: medium — fires on any Set equality; `ext x <;> simp` is close to a baseline so true non-baseline wins are unlikely (relabel will catch BASELINE_DUPLICATE).
gates.known_risks: Near-baseline; may produce BASELINE_DUPLICATE attributions rather than true SET2 wins.

gates.rationale: Bidirectional-subset route for Set equality with diff/union/inter. Speculative structural gate.
gates.expected_safety: medium — only on Set equalities; `apply Set.Subset.antisymm` fails to unify on iff goals (self-gating).
gates.known_risks: Single-line `<;>` applies the closer to both branches and breaks per-branch hypotheses; may under-solve.

mined_support.note: the constructor<;>intro<;>simp_all probe FAILED on subset_singleton_iff_eq in SF2

gates.rationale: Iff-splitting route for Set iff theorems. Speculative; the one deep-dive trial of this exact form failed.
gates.known_risks: Demonstrated insufficient on the deep-dive iff cases; expected low yield.

mined_support.note: the one win used a LOCAL hypothesis (or_iff_right_of_imp (@h x)) — not synthesizable generically

gates.rationale: Per-branch ite split. Requires synthesizing the by_cases proposition AND (in the mined win) a local hypothesis — NOT generically emittable. Hard-disabled: the wrapper will never emit this gate.
gates.expected_safety: n/a — disabled (cannot infer the binder proposition).
gates.known_risks: If ever enabled, would need binder/proposition inference and is theorem-specific (high overfit).
